Point 1 — NTM P/E is the most relevant multiple. NVDA trades at 28.2x NTM P/E — a 15% DISCOUNT to the trimmed peer median of 33.2x. This is the strongest relative-value argument: the fastest-growing company in the peer set (NTM EPS +63%) is trading cheaper than slower-growth comps on an earnings basis. Peer-median applied to NVDA NTM earnings implies a $162 target — 19% above current.

Point 2 — EV/EBITDA on NTM basis places current price near the upper end of the range ($142 high). NVDA's 65% EBITDA margin vs. peer median of 46% partly justifies a premium. At the peer-median multiple of 19.2x NVDA would be worth $102 — suggesting the market is applying roughly a 33% EBITDA-multiple premium for NVDA's margin and growth superiority.

Point 3 — EV/Revenue and P/Sales implied prices ($31-$134) bracket the current price on a wide range. The AVGO high-end (16.5x NTM EV/Rev) nearly matches current price. Revenue-multiple comps are less reliable for NVDA because its 65% EBITDA margin is 2x the peer average — revenue multiples structurally understate value for high-margin compounders.

Point 4 — Overall conclusion: NVDA is fairly valued to modestly undervalued relative to peers on a forward earnings basis (NTM P/E). On EBITDA and revenue bases the market is applying a 20-33% structural premium that is defensible given NVDA's margin profile and AI monopoly positioning. Primary valuation methodology should be DCF with explicit AI TAM build — pure comps analysis understates NVDA's intrinsic value given the absence of a true peer.
